candidates.label: Media (label point)
candidates.support: Media's location beside the Caspian Sea, on its western and southwestern sides and reaching the Zagros Mountains, is undisputed, and the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia describes it. The label point is Pleiades' point for the region.

summary.text: Media was the country beside the Caspian Sea, on its western and southwestern sides, reaching the Zagros Mountains; its chief cities included Ecbatana. Acts lists 'Medes' among the peoples present in Jerusalem at Pentecost. By this project's about AD 50 date, Media had long been part of the Parthian Empire.

history.text: The Parthian king Mithradates I (r. 165-132 BC) took Media, together with Babylonia and Elam. The Greek geographer Strabo, writing of his own day, says the Parthians ruled the Medes and the Babylonians, and in his account of AD 49 the Roman historian Tacitus records that on the death of the Parthian king Gotarzes the throne passed to Vonones, at that time 'viceroy of Media'.
